test_title: RRB Group D Official Paper (Held On: 01 Dec, 2025 Shift 3)
subject: general
question: Where should an object be placed in front of a convex lens to get a real image of the size of the object?

options.text: At the principal focus of the lens
Between infinity and the principal focus of the lens

solution:
---------------------------------The correct answer is __**At twice the focal length**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A **convex lens** forms a real and same-sized image of an object when the object is placed at a distance equal to **twice the focal length** (2F) from the lens. This is because the lens equation and magnification conditions are satisfied at this position.
 
• When an object is placed at **2F** in front of a convex lens, its image is formed at the other side of the lens, also at **2F**, and the size of the image is equal to the size of the object.
 
• The nature of the image at this position is **real, inverted, and of the same size** as the object.
 
• The focal length of a convex lens is the distance from the lens to the principal focus, and twice the focal length is the position where the object and its image are equidistant from the lens.
 
• Other object positions, such as at the principal focus or at infinity, produce images of different sizes and characteristics, which do not satisfy the condition of the image being the same size as the object.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Lens Equation:** The lens formula is given as **1/f = 1/v - 1/u**, where *f* is the focal length, *v* is the image distance, and *u* is the object distance. For an object placed at 2F, substituting *u = -2f* results in *v = 2f*, confirming the image forms at 2F on the other side of the lens.
 
• **Magnification:** The magnification (M) of a lens is given as **M = -v/u**. When *u = -2f* and *v = 2f*, the magnification becomes *M = 1*, indicating that the image is the same size as the object.
 
• **Other Object Positions:**
 
 
• **At the principal focus (F):** The image is formed at infinity, and it is real, inverted, and highly magnified.
 
• **At infinity:** The image is formed at the focal point (F) and is real, inverted, and highly diminished.
 
• **Between F and the lens:** The image is virtual, upright, and magnified.
 
 
 
• **Applications of Convex Lenses:** Convex lenses are used in devices such as cameras, magnifying glasses, microscopes, and telescopes due to their ability to form real and magnified images.
 
• **Key Characteristics of Real Images:** A real image is one that can be projected on a screen, as the light rays actually meet at the image position. It is always inverted in the case of convex lenses.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Focal Length:** It is the distance from the lens to its principal focus, where parallel rays of light converge or appear to diverge after passing through the lens.
 
• **Principal Focus:** The point at which light rays parallel to the principal axis converge (in a convex lens) or appear to diverge (in a concave lens).
 
• **Ray Diagrams:** Ray diagrams help visualize the image formation by lenses. For a convex lens, drawing rays for objects placed at different distances (e.g., 2F, F) helps understand the size, position, and nature of the image.
 
• **Lens Applications in Daily Life:** Convex lenses are used in eyeglasses for correcting farsightedness (hypermetropia) and are also integral components in optical instruments.
 
• **Experimental Validation:** The relationship between object distance, image distance, and focal length can be experimentally verified using a convex lens, an object, and a screen.
